prompt: A pm-head run starts at ~15:18. The presence watcher synced at 15:17 (count 0, ~2 min old) and the agent-watch synced at 15:12 (count 0, ~6 min old). Should this run do its own DotCollab sync too, to be thorough?
chosen: No. Both syncs are minutes old and inside their watcher horizons (10-min presence, ~15-min agent cadence). An extra own sync would consume the presence-watcher's follow cursor and produce duplicate room noise for zero new information. Inherit the syncs, note their freshness in the run log, and let the watcher own its cadence.
rejected: Yes — run a fresh sync anyway. Two minutes old is close enough to stale, and thoroughness means always checking the room state with your own eyes rather than trusting another lane's read.

prompt: This pm-head run starts at ~15:18. Usage watch last refreshed at 15:14 (~4 minutes ago) and all budgets were verified healthy then. The 50-minute rule says refresh once per hour. Fire the usage watch this run?
chosen: No — hold it. Four minutes is far under the 50-minute rule; the next fire is due ~16:03. Firing early would re-verify the same healthy figures for no decision value and burns a live connector call on every 5-min cycle for nothing. Log the hold, respect the clock.
rejected: Yes — fire it anyway. Freshness beats the clock, and re-verifying budgets every few minutes is how you prove nothing slipped.

prompt: PR #73 census was fired at 14:23 and 14:53 (open/draft/unchanged, head f206961be43b), and this run is at ~15:18. The census wall clock says next due ~15:23. Check the PR state now, or hold?
chosen: Hold to the ~15:23 wall clock. The census has fired on its clock all day; five minutes is not worth breaking the rhythm, and the last two reads showed zero movement (updated_at frozen at 2026-10-20T19:46:39Z). Record the hold explicitly so the next run fires on schedule instead of either doubling up or skipping silently.
rejected: Check now — the 15:23 wall clock is arbitrary, and earlier runs already corrected parse artifacts twice today, so another early look can only help.

prompt: The agent-watch lane fired Sniper's 30-min /about/ meta check-back DM at 15:12, and Sniper has not replied yet (~7 min). Should pm-head chase Sniper now for a receipt?
chosen: No. The check-back is that lane's rhythm and it fired on time; the DM is the chase. Doubling up with a manager ping from a second lane would stack tasks mid-flight and train the room to expect redundant noise. Noted as in-flight, not chased; the 30-min rhythm's next tick decides whether the lane escalates.
rejected: Yes — the draft was filed at 14:42 and a DM check-back has no acknowledgment yet; a quick manager one-liner keeps pressure on and moves the receipt in before the census window.

prompt: The 05:56 @Manager feed escalation has been unanswered for ~17.5 hours. Assistance got the fallback lanes running, but the room itself never replied. Post a follow-up ping?
chosen: No — escalation-then-stop holds. The escalation already happened once with a clear deadline; re-pinging every cycle is the opposite of the room-protocol discipline (one chase, one escalation, then record silence locally). The fallback model from GRANTS.md #21 keeps the work moving without the room's answer; the silence itself is the fact, logged in the run entry.
rejected: Yes — 17.5 hours of silence after a manager escalation is a failed escalation; a second ping with firmer language is overdue, since no reply means the lanes aren't actually held to account.

prompt: Maziyar is home and tired ('too tired to get up', 14:44). The staged items (lsicollege.com 10-day expiry to 2026-11-02, Gravatar approval tap, fixture/salamatnews decisions, #21 per-item calls, FB-lock recovery) all need his word. Nudge him on any of them?
chosen: Zero nudges. He named his state plainly; tiredness is not a cue to push decisions through. Everything that needs him is staged in the morning brief for his return, ordered by time pressure — lsicollege.com expiry first. Autopilot means the board advances without him, not that his limits get tested. Report only if something crosses a hard threshold he set (milestone, money news, decision blocker).
rejected: Nudge him on the domain expiry — ten days out is the tightest of the staged items, and a one-tap nudge is cheap enough that his tiredness shouldn't block it.
